records.source: וְהַנַּ֧עַר שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל מְשָׁרֵ֥ת אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י עֵלִ֑י וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה הָיָ֤ה יָקָר֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין חָז֖וֹן נִפְרָֽץ׃ס
records.gloss: And the boy Samuel [was] serving Yahweh before Eli; and [the] word of Yahweh was rare in the days those; there [was] not vision spreading out.
pieces: The boy Samuel was serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} under Eli. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was rare in those days, and visions were few.

L.1: And the boy Samuel was serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} before Eli. And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was rare in those days; there was no vision breaking out.

R.1: The boy Samuel served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Eli was in charge of him. In those days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} seldom gave anyone a message, and people seldom saw visions from God.

decisions.choice: the boy: a youth, not yet a grown man
decisions.reason: The word is used for anyone from a small child to a young man. Samuel was brought to Shiloh as a little child (1:24), and some years have passed since then (2:21, 26). The text does not give his age.

decisions.choice: serving Yahweh before Eli: helping in the sanctuary under Eli's oversight
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for priestly service at the sanctuary (2:11, 18). "Before Eli" means in Eli's presence and under his direction: Samuel serves Yahweh, and Eli is the priest in charge.

decisions.choice: rare: scarce, and so precious
decisions.reason: The word describes something costly because it is hard to find. Yahweh was speaking seldom. The chapter ends with the opposite: Yahweh revealing himself again and again at Shiloh (verse 21).

decisions.choice: there was no vision breaking out: visions were not frequent
decisions.reason: The verb means "break through" or "spread out". The phrase says that visions from Yahweh were not breaking through to his people, or were not spreading among them. Either way the point is the same: God was seldom heard from.

decisions.choice: under Eli; Eli was in charge of him; visions from God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "before Eli" means. Readable adds "from God" to show what kind of visions are meant.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} calls the boy Samuel

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְעֵלִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֣ב בִּמְקֹמ֑וֹוְעֵינָיו֙ הֵחֵ֣לּוּ כֵה֔וֹת לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And it was on the day the that, and Eli [was] lying in his place, and his eyes began [to be] dim; not he was able to see,
pieces: At that time Eli, whose sight had begun to fail so that he could not see, was lying down in his usual place,

L.2: And it happened on that day, when Eli was lying down in his place, and his eyes had begun [to be] dim; he was not able to see,

R.2: One night Eli was lying down in his usual place. His eyes were getting weak, and he could not see.

decisions.choice: his eyes: the reading the Hebrew text marks to be read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell "his eye", singular. The scribes' note in the margin says to read "his eyes", which agrees with the plural verb "they began". The pinned data follows the marked reading. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: it happened on that day: the opening of one long sentence
decisions.reason: "On that day" means "at that time", and introduces the night of Yahweh's call. The sentence that begins here describes Eli (verse 2), the lamp and Samuel (verse 3), and reaches its main event only in verse 4: "Yahweh called Samuel".

decisions.choice: his eyes had begun to grow dim: Eli was old and nearly blind
decisions.reason: Eli was very old (2:22). By 4:15 his eyes "stood" and he could not see at all. His failing sight also explains why a boy would expect to be called to help him in the night (verse 5).

decisions.choice: his usual place; One night
decisions.reason: "His place" means where he usually slept, so Balanced and Readable say "usual place". Readable says "One night" because the lamp and the lying down in verses 2-3 show that the call came at night. Readable splits the long sentence; Literal and Balanced keep it running into verse 4.

records.source: וְנֵ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ טֶ֣רֶם יִכְבֶּ֔ה וּשְׁמוּאֵ֖ל שֹׁכֵ֑ב בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם אֲר֥וֹן אֱלֹהִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: and [the] lamp of God not yet had gone out, and Samuel [was] lying in [the] temple of Yahweh, where there [was the] ark of God,
pieces: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out. Samuel lay in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where God's ark was,

L.3: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the ark of God [was],

R.3: The lamp in God's house was still burning. Samuel was lying down in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. God's ark was kept there.

decisions.choice: the lamp of God had not yet gone out: it was before dawn
decisions.reason: The lamp in the sanctuary was kept burning from evening until morning (Exodus 27:20-21; Leviticus 24:2-3). If it had not yet gone out, the night was not yet over. The words may also hint that, although Yahweh's word was rare (verse 1), his light in Israel had not gone out.

decisions.choice: the temple of Yahweh: the sanctuary at Shiloh
decisions.reason: The word means a large house or palace, and is used for Yahweh's sanctuary. This is not the later temple in Jerusalem but the house of Yahweh at Shiloh, a building with a doorpost and doors (1:9; 3:15).

decisions.choice: where the ark of God was: the sanctuary that held the ark
decisions.reason: The clause says that the ark was kept in this sanctuary. It does not say that Samuel slept beside the ark; the ark stood in the inner room, and Samuel lay somewhere within the sanctuary buildings.

decisions.choice: was still burning; was kept
decisions.reason: Readable says positively what "had not yet gone out" means and adds "kept" to make clear that the ark was stored there.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: and called Yahweh to Samuel, and he said, Here I [am].
pieces: and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel. He answered, "Here I am."

L.4: that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to Samuel, and he said, "Here I am."

R.4: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel. Samuel answered, "Here I am!"

decisions.choice: Here I am: ready to listen and serve
decisions.reason: The reply means more than "I am in this place". It is how a servant or a son answers when called, ready to do what is asked (Genesis 22:1, 11; Exodus 3:4; Isaiah 6:8).

decisions.choice: called: the main event of the sentence begun in verse 2
decisions.reason: Verses 2 and 3 set the scene; this verb is the action they lead up to.

decisions.choice: Samuel answered
decisions.reason: Readable names Samuel as the speaker, since its sentences are short and "he" could be unclear.

records.source: וַיָּ֣רָץ אֶל־עֵלִ֗י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הִנְנִי֙ כִּֽי־קָרָ֣אתָ לִּ֔י וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹֽא־קָרָ֖אתִי שׁ֣וּב שְׁכָ֑ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁכָּֽב׃ס
records.gloss: And he ran to Eli and said, Here I [am], for you called to me. And he said, Not I called; return, lie down. And he went and lay down.
pieces: He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am. You called me." But Eli said, "I did not call you. Go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.

L.5: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call; go back, lie down." And he went and lay down.

R.5: He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am. You called me." "I did not call you," Eli said. "Go back to bed." So Samuel went back and lay down.

decisions.choice: for you called me: Samuel gives the reason he has come
decisions.reason: The word "for" explains his coming. Samuel takes the voice to be Eli's, the only other person near him, and an old man who could not see might well need help at night.

decisions.choice: I did not call: Eli denies calling
decisions.reason: Eli says only that he did not call. Neither he nor Samuel yet thinks of Yahweh (verse 7).

decisions.choice: Eli said; Go back to bed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Eli as the speaker. Readable puts "go back, lie down" in everyday words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֗ה קְרֹ֣א עוֹד֮ שְׁמוּאֵל֒ וַיָּ֤קָם שְׁמוּאֵל֙ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל־עֵלִ֔י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הִנְנִ֔י כִּ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ לִ֑י וַיֹּ֛אמֶר לֹֽא־קָרָ֥אתִי בְנִ֖י שׁ֥וּב שְׁכָֽב׃
records.gloss: And again Yahweh called yet Samuel, and rose Samuel and went to Eli and said, Here I [am], for you called to me. And he said, Not I called, my son; return, lie down.
pieces: Again {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel. Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am. You called me." "I did not call, my son," Eli replied. "Go back and lie down."

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel yet again, and Samuel rose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call, my son; go back, lie down."

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel again. Samuel got up and went to Eli. "Here I am," he said. "You called me." Eli answered, "I did not call you, my son. Go back to bed."

decisions.choice: called yet again: the second of three calls
decisions.reason: The verb means "added" or "did again". The story repeats the same steps three times (verses 4-5, 6, 8) before anyone understands who is calling.

decisions.choice: my son: a kind address to a boy in Eli's care
decisions.reason: Samuel is not Eli's son. An older man could call a younger one "my son" as a sign of fatherly care (verse 16; Joshua 7:19).

decisions.choice: Eli replied; Eli answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Eli as the speaker.

records.source: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֕ל טֶ֖רֶם יָדַ֣ע אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְטֶ֛רֶם יִגָּלֶ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Samuel not yet knew Yahweh, and not yet was revealed to him [the] word of Yahweh.
pieces: Samuel did not yet know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: no word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had yet been revealed to him.

L.7: And Samuel did not yet know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not yet been revealed to him.

R.7: Samuel did not yet know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in this way. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had never yet given him a message.

decisions.choice: did not yet know Yahweh: had not yet met him through his word
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse explains the first: Yahweh had not yet spoken to Samuel. It is not a charge of unbelief. Eli's sons "did not know Yahweh" (2:12) in a different sense: they refused to honor him. "Not yet" says that Samuel's knowing is about to begin.

decisions.choice: a comment by the narrator
decisions.reason: The verse pauses the story to explain why Samuel kept running to Eli: he did not recognize the voice.

decisions.choice: in this way; had never yet given him a message
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in this way" so that young readers do not take the sentence to mean that Samuel did not believe in Yahweh, and puts "the word was revealed to him" in plain words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨סֶף יְהוָ֥ה קְרֹא־שְׁמוּאֵל֮ בַּשְּׁלִשִׁית֒ וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל־עֵלִ֔י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הִנְנִ֔י כִּ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ לִ֑י וַיָּ֣בֶן עֵלִ֔י כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קֹרֵ֥א לַנָּֽעַר׃
records.gloss: And again Yahweh called Samuel the third [time], and he rose and went to Eli and said, Here I [am], for you called to me. And understood Eli that Yahweh [was] calling the boy.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel a third time. He got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am. You called me." Then Eli realized that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was calling the boy.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel again, the third time, and he rose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And Eli understood that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was calling the boy.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called Samuel a third time. Again Samuel got up and went to Eli. "Here I am," he said. "You called me." Then Eli understood that it was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who was calling the boy.

decisions.choice: the third time: the call is completed
decisions.reason: The third call brings the pattern to its turning point. Now Eli understands.

decisions.choice: understood: came to see what was happening
decisions.reason: The verb means to discern or grasp. Eli's eyes were failing (verse 2), but he still recognized how Yahweh speaks, even though the word had become rare (verse 1).

decisions.choice: it was the LORD who was calling
decisions.reason: Readable stresses who was calling, because that is what Eli suddenly understood.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵלִ֣י לִשְׁמוּאֵל֮ לֵ֣ךְ שְׁכָב֒ וְהָיָה֙ אִם־יִקְרָ֣א אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ דַּבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁמֵ֖עַ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב בִּמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Eli to Samuel, Go, lie down; and it will be, if he calls to you, then you will say, Speak, Yahweh, for listening [is] your servant. And went Samuel and lay down in his place.
pieces: So Eli told Samuel, "Go and lie down. If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls you, then say, 'Speak, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening.'" So Samuel went back and lay down in his place.

L.9: And Eli said to Samuel, "Go, lie down, and it shall be, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls you, you shall say, 'Speak, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening.'" And Samuel went and lay down in his place.

R.9: So Eli said to Samuel, "Go and lie down. If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls you again, say, 'Speak, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening.'" So Samuel went back and lay down in his place.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of speaking of oneself
decisions.reason: The word names a slave or servant, someone who belongs to a master and does his bidding. People used it of themselves when speaking to a superior, to offer their service. Samuel is to present himself to Yahweh as one ready to obey.

decisions.choice: listening: hearing with the readiness to obey
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" often includes doing what is heard (Deuteronomy 6:4). The form describes Samuel as listening now, ready for whatever Yahweh says.

decisions.choice: if he calls you: the caller is Yahweh
decisions.reason: Eli does not name the caller in this clause, but the reply he teaches, "Speak, Yahweh", shows whom he means.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Literal keeps "slave" for this word, but here it is a humble way of speaking of oneself, not a statement about slavery, so every level has "your servant", the courtesy form set for these books (also verse 10).

decisions.choice: calls you again
decisions.reason: Readable adds "again" because the call has come three times already.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א יְהוָה֙ וַיִּתְיַצַּ֔ב וַיִּקְרָ֥א כְפַֽעַם־בְּפַ֖עַם שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל׀שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ דַּבֵּ֔ר כִּ֥י שֹׁמֵ֖עַ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃פ
records.gloss: And came Yahweh and stood and called as time at time, Samuel, Samuel. And said Samuel, Speak, for listening [is] your servant.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} stand there, and called as before, "Samuel! Samuel!" Samuel replied, "Speak, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening."

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came and stood and called as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening."

R.10: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came and stood there. He called as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had before, "Samuel! Samuel!" Samuel answered, "Speak, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is listening."

decisions.choice: came and stood: Yahweh was present, not only a voice
decisions.reason: The verbs describe a visit: Yahweh came and took his place there. Verse 15 calls what Samuel received a "vision". The text does not describe what Samuel saw.

decisions.choice: as time at time: as on the earlier occasions
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as before" (Numbers 24:1; Judges 16:20). The call came in the same way as the three before it.

decisions.choice: Samuel! Samuel!: the name said twice
decisions.reason: Calling a name twice marks a call that is urgent and personal (Genesis 22:11; 46:2; Exodus 3:4).

decisions.choice: Speak: Samuel answers without the name
decisions.reason: Eli told Samuel to say "Speak, Yahweh" (verse 9). Samuel says "Speak" without the divine name. The text does not explain why.

decisions.choice: took his stand there
decisions.reason: The verb form means to station oneself, to take a position. Balanced keeps that sense; Literal and Readable say "stood".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל הִנֵּ֧ה אָנֹכִ֛י עֹשֶׂ֥ה דָבָ֖ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּל־שֹׁ֣מְע֔וֹ תְּצִלֶּ֖ינָה שְׁתֵּ֥י אָזְנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Samuel, Behold, I [am] doing a thing in Israel which every [one] hearing it, will tingle both his ears.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Look, I am about to do something in Israel that will make both ears of all who hear of it tingle.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Look, I am doing a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Listen! I am about to do something in Israel that is so shocking that it will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.

decisions.choice: both ears will tingle: news so dreadful that it stuns the hearer
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of terrible judgments in 2 Kings 21:12 and Jeremiah 19:3. What Yahweh is about to do will shock everyone who hears of it; 4:10-22 tells what it was.

decisions.choice: I am doing: an action about to happen
decisions.reason: The participle after "look" describes something already set in motion and about to take place.

decisions.choice: a thing: an event, a deed
decisions.reason: The word can mean "word" or "thing". Here it is something Yahweh does, an event in Israel.

decisions.choice: about to do; so shocking; ring
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of "look, I am doing" with "about to". Readable says what the tingling ears mean and uses "ring", a picture young readers know.

records.heading: Judgment on Eli's family

records.source: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ אָקִ֣ים אֶל־עֵלִ֔י אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ הָחֵ֖ל וְכַלֵּֽה׃
records.gloss: On the day the that I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken against his house, beginning and finishing.
pieces: On that day I will carry out against Eli all I have said about his family, from beginning to end.

L.12: On that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, beginning and finishing.

R.12: When that day comes, I will do to Eli and his family everything I said I would do, all of it, from start to finish.

decisions.choice: all that I have spoken: the message of the man of God
decisions.reason: Yahweh has already announced the judgment on Eli's house through an unnamed man of God (2:27-36): the priesthood will pass from his family, and his two sons will die on one day (2:34). What Samuel hears confirms that word.

decisions.choice: his house: his family line
decisions.reason: "House" means Eli's household and descendants, the priestly family that was to serve Yahweh (2:30-31).

decisions.choice: beginning and finishing: completely
decisions.reason: Two verb forms side by side say that Yahweh will begin and bring to an end everything he said, leaving nothing undone.

decisions.choice: family; from beginning to end; from start to finish
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family" for "house", and turn the two verbs into an everyday phrase for completeness.

records.source: וְהִגַּ֣דְתִּי ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־שֹׁפֵ֥ט אֲנִ֛י אֶת־בֵּית֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲשֶׁר־יָדַ֗ע כִּֽי־מְקַֽלְלִ֤ים לָהֶם֙ בָּנָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א כִהָ֖ה בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And I have told to him that judging I [am] his house until forever for [the] iniquity which he knew, for bringing a curse on themselves [were] his sons, and not he restrained them.
pieces: I told him that I would bring judgment on his family forever, because of the guilt he knew about: his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.

L.13: And I have told him that I am about to judge his house forever for the iniquity that he knew, because his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.

R.13: I told Eli that I would punish his family forever because of the wrong he knew about. His sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not stop them.

decisions.choice: bringing a curse on themselves: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "cursing (or: treating with contempt) for themselves", which is an awkward phrase. The ancient Greek translation reads "speaking evil of God" here, which would mean that its Hebrew had the word for "God" where ours has "to themselves"; the two words share several letters. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a small number of places where the scribes are said to have changed a phrase so that it did not speak of cursing God outright. So the original may have said that Eli's sons were cursing God, or treating him with contempt, which fits their contempt for his offerings (2:17, 29). This translation follows the Hebrew text as it stands. This note is drawn from general knowledge of the manuscripts and the scribal lists, and must be checked against a critical apparatus.

decisions.choice: I have told him: Yahweh has already told Eli
decisions.reason: The verb form usually looks ahead ("and I will tell him", or "and you shall tell him"). Here it most likely points back to the message of the man of God (2:27-36), which Samuel's vision now confirms. But it may also announce that Yahweh is now telling Eli, through Samuel.

decisions.choice: did not restrain them: did not stop them
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebuke or hold back. Eli spoke to his sons (2:23-25) but did not stop them, and so honored them more than Yahweh (2:29). The verb comes from the same root as the word for Eli's eyes growing dim (verse 2).

decisions.choice: judging his house for the iniquity: punishing the family for its guilt
decisions.reason: "Judge" here means to pass sentence and carry it out. "Iniquity" is both the wrong done and the guilt it brings. Eli knew what his sons were doing (2:22-24); that knowledge, without action, is his guilt.

decisions.choice: guilt; the wrong they were doing; stop them
decisions.reason: Balanced says "guilt" for the word Literal renders "iniquity". Readable breaks the sentence into short ones and uses everyday words.

records.source: וְלָכֵ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְבֵ֣ית עֵלִ֑י אִֽם־יִתְכַּפֵּ֞ר עֲוֺ֧ן בֵּית־עֵלִ֛י בְּזֶ֥בַח וּבְמִנְחָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And therefore I have sworn to [the] house of Eli, if will be atoned [the] iniquity of [the] house of Eli by sacrifice and by offering until forever.
pieces: Therefore I have sworn to Eli's family that no sacrifice or offering will ever make atonement for the guilt of Eli's family."

L.14: And therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli will surely not be atoned for by sacrifice or by offering, forever."

R.14: So I have made a solemn promise to Eli's family: no sacrifice or offering will ever make atonement for their sin."

decisions.choice: if it will be atoned for: a strong "never" in an oath
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if" with nothing following it is a way of saying "surely not": the speaker leaves unsaid what should happen if the thing comes about. Yahweh swears that the guilt will never be atoned for.

decisions.choice: no sacrifice or offering: the sin was against the offerings themselves
decisions.reason: Eli's sons treated Yahweh's offerings with contempt (2:12-17, 29). The means of atonement were the very thing they despised, so they cannot cover this guilt. Eli had already warned them that no one could plead for a man who sins against Yahweh (2:25).

decisions.choice: offering: an offering of any kind
decisions.reason: The word often names the grain offering, but paired with "sacrifice" it stands for offerings in general, as in 2:17 and 2:29. Together the two words mean the whole system of offerings.

decisions.choice: guilt; sin; offering
decisions.reason: Balanced says "guilt" and Readable "sin" for the word Literal renders "iniquity". "Offering" is used rather than "grain offering" for the reason given above.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁמוּאֵל֙ עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־דַּלְת֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּאֵ֣ל יָרֵ֔א מֵהַגִּ֥יד אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֖ה אֶל־עֵלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And lay Samuel until the morning, and he opened [the] doors of [the] house of Yahweh; and Samuel [was] afraid of telling the vision to Eli.
pieces: Samuel lay there until morning, and then he opened the doors of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house. But he was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.

L.15: And Samuel lay until the morning, and he opened the doors of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.

R.15: Samuel lay in bed until morning. Then he opened the doors of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house. But he was afraid to tell Eli about the vision {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him.

decisions.choice: opened the doors: Samuel's morning duty
decisions.reason: The sanctuary at Shiloh was a building with doors (1:9). Opening them in the morning was part of the work of those who served there. Samuel goes about his duty as usual.

decisions.choice: the vision: the whole encounter of the night
decisions.reason: The word means something seen. It covers Yahweh's coming and standing (verse 10) as well as his words. It answers verse 1, where there was "no vision".

decisions.choice: afraid to tell: Samuel's fear
decisions.reason: The message was against Eli, the man who had raised him. The text says only that Samuel was afraid; verses 16-17 show that Eli had to press him.

decisions.choice: the vision the LORD had given him
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the vision.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א עֵלִי֙ אֶת־שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And called Eli Samuel and said, Samuel, my son. And he said, Here I [am].
pieces: But Eli called Samuel. "Samuel, my son!" he said. And Samuel answered, "Here I am."

L.16: And Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son!" And he said, "Here I am."

R.16: But Eli called out to him, "Samuel, my son!" Samuel answered, "Here I am."

decisions.choice: Here I am: the same answer as in the night
decisions.reason: Samuel answers Eli with the word he gave four times in the night (verses 4-6, 8). The one who taught him to answer Yahweh now calls for the message.

decisions.choice: my son: fatherly care
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Eli speaks to Samuel kindly, as a father would.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin with "But": Samuel was afraid to speak (verse 15), yet Eli called him.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־נָ֥א תְכַחֵ֖ד מִמֶּ֑נִּי כֹּ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֤ אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף אִם־תְּכַחֵ֤ד מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר מִכָּל־הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And he said, What [is] the word which he spoke to you? Do not, please, hide from me. Thus may do to you God and thus may he add, if you hide from me a word from all the word which he spoke to you.
pieces: Eli asked, "What was the message {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave you? Please do not hide it from me. May God deal with you ever so severely if you hide from me anything of all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you."

L.17: And he said, "What [is] the word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you? Please do not hide [it] from me. Thus may God do to you, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if you hide from me a word of all the word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you."

R.17: Eli asked, "What did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God punish you terribly if you keep back from me anything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you!"

decisions.choice: thus may God do to you, and thus may he add: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: This is the form of a curse called down if a promise is broken (Ruth 1:17; 1 Samuel 14:44; 20:13). The speaker leaves unsaid what "thus" will be. Eli puts Samuel under this oath to make him tell everything.

decisions.choice: he spoke: the speaker is Yahweh
decisions.reason: Eli does not name the one who spoke, but he knows from the night (verse 8) that it was Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the word: the message
decisions.reason: The same word is used three times: "the word he spoke", "a word", "all the word". Eli wants the whole message, every part of it.

decisions.choice: ever so severely; the LORD; May God punish you severely
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same form of the oath as Ruth 1:17. Readable names the LORD as the one who spoke, and says plainly what the oath means.

records.source: וַיַּגֶּד־ל֤וֹ שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א כִחֵ֖ד מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר יְהוָ֣ה ה֔וּא הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינָ֖ויַעֲשֶֽׂה׃פ
records.gloss: And told to him Samuel all the words, and not he hid from him. And he said, Yahweh [is] he; the good in his eyes he will do.
pieces: So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. Eli said, "He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees is good."

L.18: And Samuel told him all the words and did not hide [anything] from him. And he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] he; let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do what [is] good in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes."

R.18: So Samuel told him everything. He did not hide anything from Eli. Then Eli said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who decides. Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thinks is best."

decisions.choice: He is Yahweh: a statement of who God is
decisions.reason: Eli does not argue or plead. He says that the one who has spoken is Yahweh, and that this settles the matter.

decisions.choice: let him do: a wish of acceptance
alternatives: he will do what is good in his eyes
decisions.reason: The verb form can state what will happen ("he will do") or express a wish ("let him do"). Coming from Eli after a word of judgment, it is best taken as accepting Yahweh's will.

decisions.choice: good in his eyes: what he judges right
decisions.reason: "In his eyes" means in his judgment. Eli leaves the outcome to Yahweh's judgment.

decisions.choice: He is the LORD; the one who decides; what he sees is good
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the short Hebrew sentence in natural order. Readable explains why naming the LORD settles the matter, and says "whatever he thinks is best" for "what is good in his eyes".

records.source: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַֽיהוָה֙ הָיָ֣ה עִמּ֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־הִפִּ֥יל מִכָּל־דְּבָרָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And grew Samuel, and Yahweh was with him, and not he let fall from all his words to [the] ground.
pieces: Samuel grew up, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not let any of his words fall to the ground.

L.19: And Samuel grew, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him and did not let any of all his words fall to the ground.

R.19: Samuel grew up. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with him and made everything Samuel said come true.

decisions.choice: fall to the ground: fail, come to nothing
decisions.reason: A word that falls to the ground is one that is never fulfilled (Joshua 21:45; 23:14; 2 Kings 10:10). Yahweh made sure that what Samuel spoke came true.

decisions.choice: his words: Samuel's words
decisions.reason: "His" most naturally refers to Samuel, whose words Yahweh fulfilled; this is the mark of a true prophet (Deuteronomy 18:21-22), and the next verse speaks of Samuel as a prophet. It could also refer to Yahweh's own words spoken through Samuel; in the end these are the same words.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was with him: Yahweh's help and favor
decisions.reason: The phrase is said of people whom God protects and makes successful (Genesis 39:2-3; 1 Samuel 18:12, 14).

decisions.choice: made everything Samuel said come true
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of words falling to the ground and names Samuel to make clear whose words are meant.

records.heading: Samuel known as a prophet

records.source: וַיֵּ֨דַע֙ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כִּ֚י נֶאֱמָ֣ן שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל לְנָבִ֖יא לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And knew all Israel from Dan and to Beersheba that established [was] Samuel as prophet of Yahweh.
pieces: All Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was a proven prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: And all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: All the people of Israel, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south, knew that Samuel was a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who could be trusted.

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba lay in the far south, so the phrase means the whole country (Judges 20:1; 2 Samuel 24:2).

decisions.choice: confirmed: shown to be reliable
decisions.reason: The verb means to be firm, proved true, trustworthy. The same word was used in 2:35 of the "faithful priest" and the "sure house" Yahweh would raise up in place of Eli's family.

decisions.choice: prophet: one who speaks for God
decisions.reason: This is the first time the book calls Samuel a prophet: one through whom Yahweh speaks to his people.

decisions.choice: a proven prophet; a prophet who could be trusted; in the far north, in the far south
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express "confirmed" as the result: Samuel was known to be reliable. Readable adds where Dan and Beersheba lay.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥סֶף יְהוָ֖ה לְהֵרָאֹ֣ה בְשִׁלֹ֑ה כִּֽי־נִגְלָ֨ה יְהוָ֧ה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל בְּשִׁל֖וֹ בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And again Yahweh to appear in Shiloh, for revealed himself Yahweh to Samuel in Shilo by [the] word of Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} continued to appear at Shiloh, because there at Shiloh {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Samuel through the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continued to appear at Shiloh, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kept on showing {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} at Shiloh. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} known to Samuel by speaking {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word to him.

decisions.choice: continued to appear; revealed himself: the chapter comes full circle
decisions.reason: The chapter began with the word of Yahweh rare and no vision breaking out (verse 1), and with the word not yet revealed to Samuel (verse 7). It ends with Yahweh appearing again and again at Shiloh and revealing himself to Samuel.

decisions.choice: by the word of Yahweh: Yahweh made himself known through his word
decisions.reason: Yahweh's appearing took the form of his word spoken to Samuel. That word is what the verse means by his revealing himself.

decisions.choice: Shiloh: one town, spelled two ways
decisions.reason: The Hebrew spells the name of the town in two slightly different ways in this verse. Both name the same place; the meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: kept on showing himself; made himself known by speaking his word to him
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for "continued to appear" and "revealed himself", and says "his word" for "the word of the LORD".
